outlook.statement: India's response to water scarcity through river interlinking projects and large-scale inter-basin transfers will require exactly the engineering capability and project delivery experience that IHP has spent a century building. The next decade will call upon everything the company has prepared.
The shift to underground water infrastructure is both an engineering choice and a climate adaptation. Buried pipeline is inherently more resilient to climate disruption than open canal.

Operation and maintenance contracts already in IHP's portfolio are the natural direction of a company confident in what it builds. To remain responsible for a system long after commissioning is the fullest expression of the standard IHP has maintained since 1926.

Government's focus on interlinking rivers is expected to significantly expand lift irrigation schemes, creating strong demand for pipes. Growth of population and economic activities will increase water demand for domestic, industrial, agricultural, and power generation purposes. Rural water supply demand expected to increase sharply with state government development programmes.

risks: Climate assumptions on which twentieth-century water systems were designed (predictable rainfall, stable river flows, seasonal certainty) no longer hold with same reliability
Cash flow pressure from EPC model requiring working capital advanced ahead of billing and certification (experienced between FY2017-18 and 2020)
Government infrastructure funding constraints (experienced during 1990s Gulf War period)
Policy changes reserving product lines for small-scale sector (experienced in 1990s for RCC pipes)
Increased competition from medium/large scale construction entities
Availability of substitutes such as Ductile Iron pipes, spirally welded steel pipes, and H.D.P.E. pipes
Prices of key raw materials (steel, steel wires, HT wires, cement) on uptrend
Geopolitical conflict in West Asia (US-Iran) intensifying uncertainty in global energy markets, rising crude oil prices
Significant risks of high inflation due to increased costs of oil, bought-out items, and transportation impacting input expenses and overall project costs
Substantial increase in prices of steel, cement and other related products
The Company has a Risk Management Policy to identify, assess, evaluate, monitor and mitigate risks.
The risk framework defines the risk management approach across the enterprise at various levels including documentation and reporting.
The Company manages, monitors and reports on the principal risks and uncertainties that can impact its ability to achieve its strategic objectives.
The Company has a robust Risk Management framework to identify, evaluate business risks and opportunities.
The Risk Management Committee identifies internal and external risks including financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability (ESG), information, cyber security risks
Business continuity plan is part of risk management framework
